turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Hey David, what's the ETA on the checkout integration? Are we still on track for QA tomorrow?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: We're mostly on track. The frontend is almost done, but the payment API is taking a little longer than expected.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Okay. How much work is left on the backend side?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: I'd say about three or four hours, assuming I don't hit another issue with the validation.

turns.speaker: James
turns.text: What exactly is causing the delay?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: The payment provider returns a different response for some failed transactions, so I need to handle that case separately.

turns.speaker: James
turns.text: Got it. Is that something we can work around, or do we need the provider to change anything?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: We can handle it on our side. I just need to update the response mapping and add a few tests.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Okay. So do you still think the development work will be done today?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Probably, yeah. I should have the backend changes done this afternoon, but I don't want to promise a specific time until I've finished testing.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: That's fair. If development slips into tomorrow, what happens to QA?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: We'd probably need to push QA back by a few hours, unless James can get someone to review the PR quickly.

turns.speaker: James
turns.text: I can take the review as soon as the PR is ready.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Okay, that gives us a bit of room. Do we have any other dependencies?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: The only external dependency is the payment API. Everything else is already available on staging.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: And is the staging environment stable?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Yeah, as far as I know. I haven't seen any issues there today.

turns.speaker: James
turns.text: What's the main risk from your side?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: The main risk is that the payment provider has more response variations than we've seen so far.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Could that push the timeline into tomorrow afternoon?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: It could, if we find another case that needs a code change. If the current response mapping covers everything, we should still finish today.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Okay. So we're still on track, but there's not much buffer.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Exactly.

turns.speaker: James
turns.text: What if we move the lower-priority frontend task out of this sprint? That would give David more time if the API needs extra work.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: I'd rather keep the current scope if we can. Let's wait for David's next update first.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Sounds good. I'll finish the response mapping and run the tests, then I'll give you a more accurate ETA.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: When should we expect that update?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: In about two hours.

turns.speaker: James
turns.text: Perfect. If you're still on track then, I'll review the PR immediately.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Great. Let's keep QA tomorrow as the target for now, but flag it if anything changes.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Will do.
